mizutani: Ganges river
basis: name continuous; course SE as described; Mizutani, Beal, Watters; Life T50:0232c (source at Śrughna)

mizutani: Indus river
basis: name continuous; course SW as described; Mizutani, Beal, Watters, Dey; Life T50:0230c (crossing at Udakhāṇḍa)

mizutani: Amu Darya (Oxus)
basis: name continuous (waxšu); course NW; Mizutani, Vivien, Beal, Watters, Dey; Life T50:0250b

mizutani: Karashahr region: where the Yulduz-gol (海都河) from the Tianshan enters Bagrash-kul
basis: Agni = Argi/焉耆 (Henning via Mizutani); Vivien, Beal, Watters agree; no site evidence

mizutani: Bagdâd-shahr, south of Karashahr (Stein)
proposed: Bagdad-shahr S of Karashahr (Stein), or 4 li E of 四十里城子 (Huang Wenbi, via Ji)
basis: Stein via Mizutani only; Watters tentatively W of Karashahr; no description of the ruin against the 6-7 li circuit; Ji 1985 p. 49: Huang Wenbi 1958 places the Tang capital 4 li E of 四十里城子

mizutani: Kucha (庫車) region
basis: name Kuci (Lüders, Pelliot via Mizutani); Julien, Vivien, Beal, Watters agree; route 900 li = 301 km fits; Life T50:0226c

mizutani: Temple ruins on both banks of the 銅廠河 near Subashi, c. 20 km NNE of Kucha
proposed: Subashi twin ruins on both banks of the river
basis: Stein Innermost Asia p. 806 (via Mizutani): paired standing ruins either side of the river match the East/West monasteries 40+ li N; Pelliot Toch. *coguri; no rival (Beal, Watters none)

mizutani: Ruin called Duldur-Aqur, opposite Kumtura
basis: Akiyama via Mizutani; Pelliot's Tocharian B library found there (no name); position NW across river fits, Life 阿奢理兒寺 NW of city; Beal, Watters none

mizutani: Issyk-kul lake
basis: 熱海/鹹海 translate Issyk-kul 'warm lake'/Tuz-kul; extant lake long E-W, salt, ringed by mountains; Mizutani, Vivien, Beal, Watters, Cunningham; Life T50:0227a

mizutani: Sogdiana (here extended NE to 素葉 because of Sogdian trade colonies)
proposed: Sogdiana as defined by Xuanzang (Suyab to Kesh)
basis: name suɣδ; definitional region; rival views concern the form of the name only (Chavannes, Shiratori, Watters via Mizutani)

mizutani: Tashkent
basis: Chāch/Shāsh = 'stone' = 石國; Vivien, Beal, Watters agree; route from Nujkath 200 li = 34 km fits; Life names only

mizutani: Syr Darya (Jaxartes)
basis: name Iaxartes (Strabo); rises N Pamirs, flows NW as described; Mizutani, Julien, Beal, Watters; Life 葉葉河

mizutani: Ferghana valley (later Khokand)
basis: name continuous; hearsay (no 行, not in Life); Julien, Vivien, Beal, Watters; route from Chāch 1000 li = 223 km fits

mizutani: Usrūshana; capital Bunjikath = Shahristan 16 miles SW of Ura-tyube, or Ura-tyube itself
basis: Arab. Usrūshana/Sutrūshna; Vivien, Beal, Watters: Ura-tyube; Barthold/Markwart: Shahristan (via Mizutani); route from Ferghana 1000 li = 275 km fits

mizutani: Samarkand
basis: name continuous (Maracanda); Vivien, Beal, Watters, Dey, Cunningham; route from Usrūshana 500 li = 160 km (bearing 49° off); Life T50:0227c

mizutani: Afrasiab ruins on the N outskirts of present Samarkand
basis: Mongait pp. 246-48 via Mizutani: excavated capital occupied 5th c. BC to 1220; Watters: old Samarkand N/NW of the present city

mizutani: Bukhara
basis: name continuous; Vivien, Beal, Watters, Dey; route from Kharghānkath 400 li = 94 km fits on distance (bearing 29° off); capital ruin not fixed (Watters N, Mizutani NW)

mizutani: Khwarizm, both banks of the lower Amu Darya
basis: name continuous (Chorasmia); Vivien, Beal agree, Watters/Dey Khiva (inside it); route from Vadi SW 500 li = 371 km vs 120 predicted, bearing 94° off (DIST, BEARING): the figure, not the place, is wrong (Tang shu NW per Mizutani; Life W)

mizutani: Kesh = Shahr-i-sabz, c. 65 km SSW of Samarkand on the Kashka darya
basis: name continuous; Vivien, Beal, Watters; route from Samarkand 300 li = 67 km fits on distance (calibration segment), bearing 35° off

mizutani: Defile c. 10-odd km W of Derbent (Darband), 3 km long; route via Guzar and the Guzar darya valley
basis: name attested in Turkic/Arabic/Persian (Bāb al-Ḥadīd; local name Buzgala); extant narrow defile matches; Vivien, Beal, Watters agree (W of Derbent); route 500 li = 88 km fits; Life T50:0227c

mizutani: Northern Afghanistan: Pamirs to E, Persia to W, Iron Gate to N, Hindu Kush to S, Oxus through the middle; the extent is not generally agreed
basis: name continuous; Xuanzang's own bounds; Vivien, Beal, Watters, Dey agree on the region

mizutani: Termez (Tirmidh), on the Amu Darya at the Soviet-Afghan border
basis: name continuous; N bank of Oxus fits; Vivien, Beal, Watters; hearsay (not in Life); Ji 1985 p. 104: 1964-66 excavations at Old Termez (Kushan stupas, Kara-Tepe cave monastery, Brahmi/Kharosthi sherds)

mizutani: Dushanbe (formerly Stalinabad), capital of Tajikistan
basis: Shūmān of the Islamic geographers (Julien, Vivien, Beal); town site less firm (Beal adds Kulab; Vivien SE of Chaghaniyan); hearsay, no figures

mizutani: Khuttal, between the Wakhsh and the Panj; capital Hulbuk on the Amu Darya
basis: name continuous; Julien, Vivien, Beal agree on Khuttal; hearsay, no figures; Ji 1985 p. 111: chief town Kulab

mizutani: Darwāz district on the Panj (upper Amu Darya); capital Kala-i-khum
basis: Kumādh/Komēdōn; Beal: Darwaz or Rasht; Julien, Vivien tentative nearby; Oxus SW and Śikini S suit Darwaz; hearsay

mizutani: Baghlān in the Kunduz (Surkhab) river valley, c. 60 km SW of Kunduz
basis: name continuous; Vivien, Beal agree; SW of Kunduz fits; hearsay

mizutani: Khulm: ruins N of present Tashkurgan
basis: name continuous; Vivien (ruins 5 mi from Tashkurgan), Beal; on the Kunduz-Balkh road

mizutani: Balkh (ancient Bactria)
basis: name continuous; Julien, Vivien, Beal, Watters, Dey, Cunningham; Life T50:0228a; route z +2.8 to Gaz is due to 01.36's point; Foucher I p. 60: rampart survey 1924, Bala-Hisar = the pilgrims' royal city

mizutani: Nau-bahār of the Islamic geographers; its stupa probably Top-i-Rustam (excavated by Foucher)
proposed: Nau-bahār at Balkh; stupa probably Top-i-Rustam
basis: name Nau-bahār in the Islamic geographers; Foucher's excavation of Top-i-Rustam (via Mizutani), no naming find; Life T50:0228b same relics; Foucher I pp. 84, 96: his excavation 1924 proved Top-e-Rustam a Buddhist stupa restored before 630; monastery/vihara not found, layout does not match the text

mizutani: Sar-i-pul on the Ab-i-Safid, c. 100 km SW of Balkh (Islamic Anbār)
basis: only Beal's tentative 'near Sir-i-pul'; the name gives it no support: Marquart's Zumathān (via Ji) a weak fit (y- for z, -ān unwritten; data/names/); Vivien no synonym, Watters none; Life T50:0228b confirms a visit SW of Balkh

mizutani: Darrah Gaz (Tamaris valley), S of Balkh up the Darrah Yusuf
proposed: Darrah Gaz at the valley mouth c. 30 km S of Balkh (Beal's 20 mi)
basis: name Gaz/Gachi; Beal, Mizutani (Foucher); route: mapped point in Dara-i-Suf (94 km) z +2.8 for 'S 100 li', Beal's 32 km z +0.6 and chain_best; same place, point should move north

mizutani: Bamiyan valley between the Hindu Kush and Koh-i-Baba
basis: name continuous; standing colossi match (01.37.01, 01.37.01a); Vivien, Beal, Watters, Cunningham; route from Gaz 600 li = 138 km fits; Life T50:0228c

mizutani: The 53 m Buddha at Bamiyan
basis: standing rock-cut colossus NE of the city, 140-150 chi, matches; Vivien, Beal, Watters (Talbot 173 ft), Majumdar (180 ft); Life 150 chi

mizutani: Burdj-i-Abdallah enclosure at the N end of Begram site (Foucher's 'old city')
proposed: area of Burj-i-Abdallah, N end of Begram (building unidentified)
basis: Foucher via Mizutani (area only); Beal: S bank of the river NW of the capital, perhaps the Ghorband; depends on Begram (01.38a)
